title: Dialogue search: find the line, land on the scene, clip it
description: Depends on the transcription stage. Server: at transcript time also parse the VTT into cues (start, end, text) into a library.db table (cues: item id, start, end, text) with an FTS5 index; GET /api/search?q= gains a 'lines' group — up to 20 cues whose text matches, each {item envelope fields, start, end, text, links.self pointing at the item, and a `passage` {t: start-2, end: end+2} the client can spell as a hash}; the item document gains links.lines (GET /api/items/{id}/lines?q=) for the in-page finder. Client: the search results draw the lines group with the text, the work and a time; a tap opens #/item/<id>?t=&end= (a passage, so it plays the scene and stops); the item page gets a 'Find in dialogue' box above Details when links.lines exists, listing hits the same way. Goldens (search.json with a cue row, item-film.json) refreshed. Files: internal/store (cues + FTS), internal/pipeline/transcribe.go (parse), cmd/server/search.go, hyper.go, route.go, web/renderers.js, web/kernel.js, web/index.html.

title: A transcription stage: whisper.cpp gives every silent file subtitles
description: The one Plex and Netflix cannot do for your own files. A post-scan stage after trickplay, in internal/pipeline (the only package that shells out): when TRANSCRIBE names a whisper.cpp binary (whisper-cli) and WHISPER_MODEL a model file, for each video or audio item with no subtitle track of its own, extract 16kHz mono wav with ffmpeg from the presigned URL, run whisper with -ovtt, and store the WebVTT under data/subs/<id>/transcript.vtt; write a row in library.db (transcripts: item id, language, generated_at, model) so the item document lists it as a subtitle track {ordinal: 'transcript', title: 'Transcript (generated)', supported: true, href: the same .vtt route}, served by the existing subtitles handler. The stage yields to live playback exactly like trickplay, runs one item at a time, is disabled without the env vars, and never re-runs for an item that has a transcript unless its etag changed. Tests: BuildArgs-style pure argv test for the whisper and extract commands, a store test, and the item document with a transcript (a golden row in the fixture). README design note. Files: internal/pipeline/transcribe.go (+ test), internal/store, cmd/server/main.go, hyper.go.

title: My List: save a work for later, a shelf on the home
description: Netflix's My List, YouTube's Watch later. Server: state.db gains a saved table (profile, work key, saved_at); the work document and library tiles carry a `save` / `unsave` action for the asking profile (POST/DELETE /api/list/{key}); GET /api/list?client_id= answers the shelf as tiles newest first; the root names it links.list; a kid profile's list is filtered like the shelves; the library document carries `list` = the shelf so the home draws it without a second fetch. Table-tested store + handler; goldens (root, library, work-*, both halves). Client: a bookmark control on the work pane and on tile hover/focus (drawn from the action), a 'My List' row on the home after Continue. Files: internal/store, cmd/server (a new list.go + test, hyper.go, library.go), web/renderers.js, web/kernel.js, web/index.html.

title: Skip intro and skip credits, from the chapter names the file already carries
description: Netflix's button without detection: many rips carry chapters named Intro / Opening / Titles and Credits / End Credits. Server: the item document's media_info.chapters stays as it is, but the play session document gains `skips`: [{kind: 'intro'|'credits', start, end}] derived from chapter titles (case-insensitive match on intro, opening, titles, credits, end credits; end = next chapter start or duration), so the client is told rather than taught the rule — table-test the derivation. Client: while the position is inside an intro skip, a 'Skip intro' button overlays the picture's lower right and seeks to its end; when the position enters a credits skip and the session has links.next, the up-next countdown starts then (showUpNext) rather than at the natural end. Golden refresh (session-play.json, both halves). Files: cmd/server/session.go (+ test), web/player.js, web/renderers.js (session chrome), web/index.html.

title: Mark as watched / unwatched, from the item page and every episode row
description: Plex's most-used context action. Server: the item document gains a `watched` action (POST /api/items/{id}/watched with {"watched": true|false}) that writes the position to the duration (watched) or clears the row (unwatched) for the asking profile — one handler, table-tested, refused with passage-on while a passage is live like any progress write; member envelopes in a work carry it too so a row can offer it. Client: a small ✓ / ↺ control on the item page beside Play (drawn from the action, its label the server's: "Mark watched" / "Mark unwatched") and on each episode row in the show pane (renderers.js memberRow, right-aligned, stopPropagation so the row's own tap does not fire); after it answers, the kernel forgets and re-reads the view so ticks and Next up move. Goldens refresh (work-show, item-film, both halves). Files: cmd/server/hyper.go, a new cmd/server/watched.go + test, web/renderers.js, web/kernel.js, web/index.html.

title: EPIC: the killer features — what Plex, Netflix and YouTube taught the house
description:
The features people reach for in Plex, Netflix and YouTube that this architecture makes cheap: the server already knows genres, chapters, per-profile positions, arrival dates, live sessions and trickplay sprites, so most of these are a document field plus a renderer. Filed as thin slices in four waves, grouped so the agents of one wave touch different files. Every slice: the gate (gofmt, vet, build, go test, node --check, node --test), goldens refreshed in both halves when a document changes, the renderer rules (no URL composed in renderers.js/player.js, no video element from a renderer), and the browser smoke before the wave's PR.

Wave 1: playback speed, sleep timer, number keys; mark watched/unwatched and remove from Continue; New episodes, Because you watched, household activity.
Wave 2: skip intro/credits from chapter names, loop a passage, chapter names on the scrub hover and a chapter list with thumbnails; My List; subtitle appearance and hover previews.
Wave 3: a transcription stage (whisper.cpp behind an env var) that gives every silent file subtitles.
Wave 4: dialogue search over the transcripts, landing on the line and minting a clip of it.

title: Playback speed on the transport, the mini-player and the lock screen
description: YouTube and every audiobook app have it; a 1.5x audiobook is the single most asked feature. Add a speed control (0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2) to the player's control row and the mini-player, applied as playbackRate on the media element (hls.js follows it); remember the choice per medium in localStorage (audio and video separately — a 1.5x audiobook should not make the next film fast). Keyboard: Shift+. / Shift+, step it, like YouTube. Media Session's positionState carries playbackRate. While casting, the RemotePlayerController has no rate API in the default receiver: hide the control and leave the rate alone. The '?' help card lists the keys. Files: web/player.js, web/renderers.js (miniPlayer), web/index.html.

title: Casting: theatre mode stays off and the controls never fade while the page is the remote
description: Two wave-3 slices met badly: theatre mode (flickr-duw.14) puts body.theatre on for any video item and fades #player-title/#transport after 3s idle while isPlaying(), which is cast-aware; the cast remote (flickr-duw.17) hides the video and shows #cast-remote in its place. Result while casting: the title bar and transport are absolutely positioned over the remote card (covering artwork and Stop casting on >640px), and the remote's controls fade out. Fix in web/player.js: attach() toggles body.theatre only when not casting(); wake() never arms the idle timer while casting() and removes .idle; onCastConnectionChanged() re-evaluates both (toggle theatre, wake) after the connect/disconnect; toggleFullscreen() and the f key are a no-op while casting. No CSS change needed beyond what falls out.

title: Home hero and detail backdrop; genres, runtime and certification on the detail page
description: Depends on ux07 (links.backdrop, runtime_minutes, certification, cast). Do, web/renderers.js + web/index.html: the library's home leads with a hero — the continue shelf's first entry, else the first recently-added, else the first tile — drawn with its backdrop as a full-width image with a gradient, the title, a one-line overview and its primary action (resume/play) taken from that entry's own document actions; the item page paints links.backdrop behind #detail-info with a gradient into the page, and shows genres as chips, runtime (formatted h m), certification as a small badge and 'With: A, B, C' from cast. Every address is copied from the document. Lazy-load images with a placeholder colour. Keep render tests green. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: Home has a hero with backdrop and one primary action. Detail page shows backdrop, genres, runtime, certification, cast when present, nothing when absent.

title: Audio keeps playing while you browse: a persistent mini-player bar
description: The media element persists by design, but kernel.js applyRoute() calls closeStage() whenever the routed item is not the playing one, so leaving an album or audiobook page kills playback. Do: for medium 'audio' (music and audiobooks) navigation no longer closes the stage; instead the session chrome collapses into a fixed bottom mini-player bar (cover, title · work, play/pause, ±30s, a thin progress line, and a tap that navigates back to the item's hash, which restores the full chrome). Video keeps today's rule (leaving stops). Starting any other item, or Stop, closes the sitting. The bar is rendered by a new Render.miniPlayer(session, ctx) (pure; test it in render_test.mjs; no <video> emitted, the device element is moved into a hidden slot in the bar so the buffer survives). kernel.js gains the rule; player.js attach() handles the two chrome shapes. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: Play a track, tap Back, browse the library: the music continues and a mini-player shows; tapping it returns to the full player without a reload of the stream. Video still stops on leaving.

title: Theatre mode: keyboard shortcuts, auto-hiding controls, immersive layout
description: Only the reader binds keys; the player has none; nothing auto-hides; the video is boxed at 58vh with the back button, now-playing and status around it. Do, web/player.js + web/index.html: keyboard — space/k play-pause, ←/→ ±10s, j/l ±30s, ↑/↓ volume, m mute, f fullscreen, c cycle subtitles, n next member, Escape leaves fullscreen or backs out (ignore when a text input has focus); auto-hide — while playing and the pointer is idle 3s over #device, controls and the cursor fade out, any movement/tap brings them back, paused state always shows them; immersive layout — the stage gets a dark backdrop, the video may take the full viewport width and up to ~80vh on wide screens, the back button and now-playing become an overlay title bar at the top that hides with the controls. A small '?' in the controls lists the shortcuts. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: All shortcuts work and do nothing while typing. Controls fade after 3s of playback idle and return on movement. The player fills the width with an overlay title bar.

title: Show pane: seasons, watched ticks, progress bars and a Next up lead
description: Every season lands in one list; episode rows draw no watched state or progress though members carry 'resume'; the work's progress.next is named but not used. Do, server: a show's member envelopes carry season and episode numbers (from identity) and 'watched: true' when position >= 90% of duration (same rule internal/works uses); refresh goldens. Client, renderers.js showPane(): a 'Next up' card at the top (poster/still, label, a primary play control taken from the work's play action), then episodes grouped by season with a heading per season (tabs when more than one; a season row is collapsible), each row with a check mark when watched and a thin progress bar when resume exists; extras keep their own section. Replace the amber #show-note with the progress text under the title. CSS in index.html. Keep render tests green; add a test for the grouping. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: Show pane groups by season, shows watched ticks and progress bars, leads with Next up. Goldens carry season/episode/watched. Tests green.

title: The player owns its transport: native controls off, fullscreen, tap to pause, double-tap to seek
description: The video keeps its 'controls' attribute and a custom scrub bar and button row sit under it: two transports. Fullscreen exists only on the native bar, so going fullscreen loses chapter ticks, passage flags and trickplay previews; the custom row has no fullscreen and no mute. Do, in web/player.js build()/bindDevice() and web/index.html: remove the 'controls' attribute; add a fullscreen button that calls requestFullscreen() on the #device wrapper (so the scrub bar and overlays survive) with CSS for :fullscreen (video fills, controls overlay at the bottom over a gradient); a mute button beside the volume slider; click on the video toggles play/pause; on touch, a double tap on the left/right third seeks -10/+30 with a brief on-screen ripple; the scrub bar handles pointer events (touch drag) not only click; the 'vol' text label becomes an icon. Keep the tap-to-play overlay. Cast and audio-mode behaviour unchanged. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: No native controls. Fullscreen keeps the custom scrub bar with ticks/flags/previews. Tap toggles pause, double-tap seeks on touch, mute works, scrub drags on touch.

title: Home: the library renders its bands as rows with headings, Continue first, Recently added second
description: GET /api/library already orders tiles in bands (shows, films, artists, audio works, books) but the grid draws them as one wall. Do: library tiles gain a 'band' field on the server (cmd/server/library.go: 'tv', 'movies', 'music', 'audiobooks', 'books' — a file the path could not place lands in its medium's band) and the library document carries 'bands' as an ordered list of {key, title}. web/renderers.js library() draws: the continue shelf, then a 'Recently added' row from doc.recently_added when present (flickr-duw.8), then one section per band with a heading and its tiles as a grid; search and genre still filter within sections and an empty section disappears. The 'N titles' count goes. CSS in web/index.html. Refresh goldens (both halves); keep render tests green. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: Home shows headed sections in server order; empty sections hidden; search filters within sections; goldens and tests updated.

title: Item page: admin actions under Details, and 'Fix the identity' gets a form from its input sketch
description: restControls() draws 'Fix the identity' and 'Probe this file again' as peers of Play. The identity button is broken: the kernel's default invoke (player.js invoke → default) posts no body, so it can never succeed. Do: on the item page the identity/reprobe/enrich controls move inside the Details disclosure (flickr-duw.3 adds it; if it is not merged yet, add the disclosure here). The identity control opens a small inline form built from the action's 'input' sketch (kind, title, year, season, episode, part, author, track_title — types from the sketch, current values from doc.identity) and submits JSON to the action's href; a Problem shows in the toast; on success the view is re-read (K.forget(); K.applyRoute()). Put the form builder in renderers.js (pure: sketch + current → HTML) and the submit in kernel.js. Test the form builder in render_test.mjs. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: Play stands alone on the item page. Identity form submits a body matching the sketch and refreshes the view. Test covers the form builder.

title: Responsive layout: phone breakpoints, 44px touch targets, visible focus rings
description: There is not one @media rule. On a phone the header wraps into rows, buttons are ~30px tall, #detail-info's 180px poster sits beside text, the reader's .rd-toc is a fixed 260px column, and no :focus-visible style exists. Do, in web/index.html and web/audio.css: (1) a max-width: 640px breakpoint — grid minmax 110px, header compact, #detail-info stacks with the poster centred at ~40vw, #controls / #doc-controls wrap with larger buttons, the continue row cards 110px; (2) all buttons/selects at least 44px tall on coarse pointers (@media (pointer: coarse)); (3) a :focus-visible outline using the accent colour on every interactive element (buttons, .card, .item, .cw-card, links, selects); (4) the reader TOC becomes an overlay drawer under 640px (it already toggles hidden; position it absolute over .rd-view). Also add a max-width: 1400px centring for very wide screens. CSS only. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: At 375px width nothing overflows horizontally, header fits in one or two rows, targets are ≥44px on touch. Keyboard tab shows a focus ring on cards and buttons. Reader TOC overlays on phones.

title: Server: no file name is ever a title — display titles for audio parts, films and episodes
description: The item document's title for an audiobook part is '01 - Part 1.m4b' (see cmd/server/testdata/hyper/continue.json), a film's label is 'Frozen.mkv', an extra's label is 'Deleted Scenes.mkv'. They reach the detail heading, now-playing and the continue shelf. Do, in cmd/server/hyper.go (itemDoc) and internal/works (ItemLabel): title is the work's title for a single-member work, the episode's TMDB title else 'Episode N' for an episode, the track_title for a track, 'Part N' (or the chapter title) for an audiobook part, the book title for a book; a member's label keeps its structured form ('S03E22 · Beach Games', 'Track 7 · Karma Police', 'Part 2'). An extra's title is its file stem with the extension removed and underscores/dots turned to spaces. Add a  field (the object key's base name) on the item's own page so the name is still reachable. Table-test it. Refresh goldens with go test ./cmd/server -update (both halves). Update web/render_test.mjs if it pins a title. No client change needed beyond tests.
acceptance_criteria: No golden carries a title ending in a media extension. Table test covers movie, episode, track, audiobook part, book, extra. go test ./... and node tests green.

title: Tiles show a title and one subtitle; the tech line moves to a details disclosure on the item page
description: Every tile prints a monospace tech line ('1920x816 h264/ac3 · 8.40 GB · 3 ch'); episode rows use it as their metadata line; the detail page prints it under the overview. Do: card() in web/renderers.js stops drawing .c-tech (the text tile with no artwork may keep tech as its small subline since it has nothing else). memberRow() shows the member's label and, when it has one, its duration (fmtTime) or overview — not tech. The item page gets a <details> 'Details' block near the bottom holding: the tech line, the object key/label (file name), the identity kind, and the media_info summary. Keep render_test.mjs green (check what it asserts about tech). CSS in web/index.html. Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE.
acceptance_criteria: No tile or episode row shows codec/size text. Item page has a collapsed Details disclosure with the tech line. Tests green.

title: Header: name, search, profile. Presets, scan and the hardware badge move into a settings panel
description:
The header today carries the app name plus 'media server PoC', the 'Play as' capability preset select, the Scan button, its polling status line and the HW badge. Those are engineering controls and every viewer sees them on every screen. The <title> says 'flickr — media PoC'.

Do: the header becomes the name (just 'flickr'), the search box (moved up from #lib-bar; it keeps filtering the library the way it does today and is hidden on views that are not the library) and the profile chip. A gear button opens a settings panel (a fixed drawer or a modal, same style as the profile gate) that holds: the capability preset select, the Scan button and its status text, the hardware badge and its trace as a tooltip or a list, and the autoplay-next toggle (currently a button in the transport row, player.js setAutoplay — leave the player's copy working; the panel may simply host the same button or a duplicate that calls the same setter through a small Player API). <title> becomes 'flickr'. Scan status polling stays as it is but writes into the panel.

Files: web/index.html (markup + CSS), web/kernel.js (boot wiring, scan status target), possibly web/player.js (caps() reads #profile — keep that id so nothing else changes). Do NOT bump sw.js CACHE; the integrator bumps once per wave. Keep web/kernel_test.mjs green (it asserts one /api/ literal and one line of logic in index.html).
acceptance_criteria: Header shows only name, search and profile chip. Presets, scan, HW badge live in a settings panel opened by a gear. Tab title is 'flickr'. Scan still runs and reports. node --test web/*_test.mjs green.

title: EPIC: flickr feels like a killer app — the UI stops being an engineer's console
description:
UX analysis, 2026-09-07. The engine underneath is killer-app grade: pure playback decisions, resume, up-next, chapters, trickplay, subtitles, cast, EPUB/PDF reading, profiles and passages all work, and the hypermedia documents mean most of the UI work is renderers and CSS. What is missing is the feeling: a home screen that says what to watch next, a player that becomes a theatre, audio that keeps playing while you browse, and a layout that works on a phone.

What reads as a demo today: the tab title says PoC; the header carries the capability presets, a scan button with a polling status line and a hardware badge; every tile, episode row and detail page prints a codec/size line; every play prints a decision trace; the home screen is one undifferentiated grid with no headings, hero or recently-added; shows are one flat list with no seasons, watched ticks or next-up; the player keeps the native controls attribute AND a custom row (two transports, fullscreen only on one, no keyboard shortcuts); navigating away stops music and audiobooks; there is not one media query; admin actions render as peers of Play; "Fix the identity" posts no body; file names leak into titles.

Each child is a thin slice that merges alone. Ordering is by wave (in the child notes), so slices that touch the same files land one after another. Every slice: `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, `node --check web/*.js`, `node --test web/*_test.mjs`. The renderer rules hold (no URL composed in renderers.js/player.js, no <video> from a renderer); a document change refreshes both golden halves with `go test ./cmd/server -update`.

title: hyper 6: the client kernel and renderers — index.html split under the contract, goldens shared with Go
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The client. web/index.html becomes: kernel.js (splitHash → /api/-/route → render(view, document); hashchange; the persistent <video> and reader container), renderers/*.js (library, work, artist, item, session, continue — pure functions of an envelope, a control per actions entry, never composing a URL), player.js (the device: media element, hls.js, cast, position tick, scrub, chapter ticks, end-of-passage pause, tap-to-play). Old JSON shapes and the flat /api/items read leave the client. JS tests under node --test over the Go goldens in testdata/ (copied by a go test that fails when they drift). The shell list and sw.js bump; the CI check from flickr-ake (a shell file changed without a cache bump fails the gate) lands here.
close_reason: PR #21 merged: kernel/renderers/player, index.html 2267→332, shared goldens, 87 node tests, headless smoke 32/32

title: hyper 4: sessions are documents; a passage is session state; the 409; marks and minting server-side
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §Passages are session state. POST /api/items/{id}/play takes an optional passage {t,end,until,from,to}; answers a session envelope (GET /api/sessions/{id} too): url, method, decision trace, passage resolved (item ids, ends_at), actions progress / keep_watching / stop / next / mark_in / mark_out / link. POST progress during a passage → 409 problem+json type passage-on, remedy keep_watching; after keep_watching → 200. Direct-play sessions get a session row too (today only transcodes have ids). mark_in/mark_out post positions; actions.link and GET /api/-/passage?… answer the minted link and its sentence ('S03E22 2:22 – 14:14 of Beach Games'); the server snaps to chapters. Handler tests for the three rules. Client: setPassage/markBounds/passageLink/keepWatching read the session document; web/passage.js shrinks to the clock predicates (passageEnded, textPassageEnded); the 'End of the passage' panel renders actions.keep_watching and links.back. sw.js bump.
close_reason: PR #18 merged: session documents, passage as session state, the 409, marks and minting server-side, work-form passage minting

title: hyper 3: GET /api/library and GET /api/artists/{name}; the browser stops regrouping
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The documents. GET /api/library: tiles in server order (shows, films, artist shelves, audio works, books), genre facets, each tile an envelope with links.self and links.artwork and a summary line; GET /api/artists/{name}: albums in year order with covers. Golden tests. Client: buildLibrary and audio.js's works()/artists() grouping deleted; renderGrid/renderShow/renderArtist read the documents; search filters the library document client-side (a filter, not a regrouping). GET /api/works/{key} (hyper 1) feeds the show and album panes. sw.js bump.
close_reason: PR #17 merged: /api/library and /api/artists/{name} documents, client regrouping deleted

title: hyper 1: internal/hyper envelope + root, item and work documents
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The envelope and §The documents. New package internal/hyper: Envelope, Link, Action (method, href, input sketch, label), Problem (RFC 7807 with remedy), a Doc builder; WriteDoc/WriteProblem helpers. New handlers: GET /api/ (root: profile, links to library/continue/artists/scan/system, action scan), GET /api/items/{id} (the missing route: media_info, chapters, subtitles, artwork links, links.work/prev/next, actions play/read/progress/identity/reprobe/enrich with unavailable+reason where a kind lacks one), GET /api/works/{key} (fields, members as item envelopes with chapters/sections, places as tokens WITH labels — episodes S02E05 0:00 'The Fight', chapters 1:19:00 'Chapter 03', sections ch. 7 'The Cellar' — the profile's progress, actions play/read/passage). Golden JSON tests under testdata/ per document kind (a film, a show, an audiobook, an album, a book), driven from an in-memory store. Existing routes untouched; no client change. Note for the waymark side: /-/places-style tokens now carry labels; waymark-z8u4's follow-up (a label slot in the :places recipe) can read them.
close_reason: PR #15 merged: internal/hyper envelope, root/item/work documents with labelled places, goldens

title: hyper 2: internal/passage grammar + GET /api/-/route resolves every hash
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §Routes are resolved by the server. New package internal/passage: the grammar now in web/passage.js (splitHash-equivalent query parse, t/end/until/untilEp/ep/from/to, locators cfi:/ch:/pg:/pct:, episode codes), table-tested with the same cases as web/passage_test.mjs. New GET /api/-/route?hash=<hash>: answers {view: library|work|artist|item, document: <envelope from hyper 1>, passage: resolved or null, autoplay: bool}; resolves #/show/<title>?ep=S03E22 against the show's members, #/item/<id>, #/artist/<name>, #/, and text locators against a book's sections; an unknown title or episode is a problem+json whose remedy links the library or the show. Every hash spelling in README 'Deep links and passages' is a test row. Client: the router's parseRoute/applyRoute call the route document instead of parsing (minimal change: keep renderers as they are, feed them what the server answered); resolveShowPassage/findEpisode leave the client. sw.js bump.
close_reason: PR #16 merged: internal/passage grammar, GET /api/-/route with every hash spelling, client router asks the server

title: EPIC: flickr's own hypermedia envelope — the server says what exists and what may be done; the browser renders and owns the device
description: Design: docs/hypermedia.md (decision 2026-09-07: backend-driven with flickr's own envelope, not a waymark application). Every document is {self, kind, fields…, links, actions, unavailable}; errors are RFC 7807 problem+json with a remedy; the client follows links and actions and knows only /api/ by heart. Routes resolve on the server, passages are session state with the three rules enforced there, grouping and minting leave the browser. Eight children in order; each ships green behind the existing routes until step 6 switches the client.
close_reason: All eight steps merged (PRs #14–#22): envelope, route resolution, library/artist documents, sessions with passage state, reader sessions, client kernel, cast bridge, README. Follow-ups: flickr-bqx, flickr-svh, flickr-aae

title: Text reads: epub books in a reader, with a locator, a fraction and passages
description: Depends on the model bead. The epub prober fills out: OPF metadata (title, creator, language, cover → data/covers/), the spine and the TOC (nav.xhtml or NCX) as Sections {order, href, title}; a reader pane in web/ on epub.js (pinned, vendored under web/vendor so the LAN-only engine loads nothing from the internet at read time) that opens the book from GET /api/items/{id}/book (the epub bytes, range-capable) and reports position as an epub CFI plus the book's own percentage — the locator rides playback_state in a new nullable locator TEXT column beside position_seconds, and the fraction law gets its text unit: progress_text 'ch. 7 · 34%' with progress 0.34; passages: #/item/<id>?from=<locator>&to=<locator> where a locator is cfi:<epubcfi>, ch:<section order> or pct:<0..1> — the reader opens at from and, on reaching to, shows 'end of the passage' and stops advancing, writing no progress while in passage mode. PDF is its own bead.

title: Passage sessions in the player: start there, stop there, and never move the person's saved place
description: The deep-link grammar, stable and documented in README: #/item/<id>?t=<start_seconds>&end=<end_seconds> for audio/video; &until=<item_id> bounds an episode run (auto-advance stops after that item); text passages are ?from=<locator>&to=<locator> (the reader bead honours them; this bead parses and passes them through). Player behaviour: (1) t wins over saved progress — playItem(item, startAt) already takes a start; (2) at end the player pauses, fires no up-next and shows 'end of the passage' with a 'keep watching' button that leaves passage mode; (3) the scrubber marks both ends; (4) a passage session writes NO progress — neither POST /api/progress on pause/end nor the natural-end write — because a scene replayed for a talk is not where the person is in the film (guard every write site with a passageActive flag; test the guard in main_test where progress is posted); (5) cast: castLoad carries t and the receiver is told the end (or the sender polls and stops it). One item first; episode runs via until. Keep the URL the single source of truth: parseRoute reads the query part of the hash.

On the item page, the chapters wrap of buttons becomes a list with a thumbnail per chapter cut from the trickplay sprite sheet (links.trickplay's index gives sheet_hrefs, cols, rows, interval_seconds and tile size; the kernel fetches the index once per item and the renderer takes it as ctx) and the chapter's title and time; a tap plays from there as today. Files: web/player.js (hover), web/renderers.js (item), web/kernel.js (index fetch into ctx), web/index.html.

title: Household activity under the gear: who is playing what, right now
description: Plex's dashboard, one row per live session. Server: GET /api/activity answers the live play and read sessions (profile, item title and work, method, position from the last progress write or the transcode's fetched time, started_at) — the root names it as links.activity; a small golden. Client: an 'Activity' section in the settings panel that reads it when the panel opens and refreshes every 5s while open. Files: cmd/server (a new activity.go + test, hyper.go root link), web/kernel.js, web/index.html.

title: Number keys seek to tenths, comma and period step a frame
description: YouTube's: 0..9 seek to that tenth of the duration; , and . step one frame (1/fps from media_info.fps, 1/25 when unknown) while paused. Add them to the player's keydown beside the existing shortcuts (respect the same guards: not while typing, not for the reader), and to the SHORTCUTS table the '?' card draws. Files: web/player.js.

title: Search results include artist shelves
description: GET /api/search groups works, episodes, tracks, parts and books; an artist name matches nothing as itself. Add an 'artists' group (the same tiles the library draws, so R.hashFor opens the shelf), matched on the artist's name. Handler test row, golden refresh (search.json, both halves), and Render.search draws the group like the others.

title: Ten-foot mode focuses the first tile on a route change, and arrows wrap at row ends
description: flickr-duw.23: the focus ring only appears on the first arrow press, and Right at the end of a row is a no-op. On a route change in ten-foot mode, focus the first focusable in #view (after the swap settles, i.e. after mount's promise). In Focus.pick, when nothing lies in the arrow's direction on the same row, wrap to the first element of the next row (Right) or the last of the previous (Left). Table-test the wrap in web/focus_test.mjs.

title: Profiles pick a face at the gate
description: flickr-duw.22 assigns a deterministic emoji server-side. The gate's create row gets a small row of faces to pick from (a fixed list rendered by the kernel from what the server offers: add an 'avatars' list to the root document's create_profile action input sketch or a links.avatars — keep it the server's list), the pick is sent as avatar on create, and the server keeps assigning one when none is sent. Goldens refresh if the root changes.

title: Episode stills and the Next up art get the shimmer placeholder too
description: flickr-duw.20's placeholder covers .poster-wrap tiles and #detail-poster only; img.still in episode rows and the Next up card's picture pop in bare. Extend the CSS and the kernel's load/error marking to those images (a wrapping element or the img itself gets .loaded).

title: Clip handles have a keyboard path
description: The clip grips (flickr-duw.21) are pointer-only. Give each .clip-handle tabindex=0 and role=slider with aria-valuenow/min/max; Left/Right move the focused grip by 1s (Shift: 10s) and post the mark on keyup the way a pointer release does; Enter on the Share button already works. A visible focus ring comes from the existing :focus-visible rules.

title: Search box clears when leaving the results route
description: The header search box keeps its text after leaving #/search/<q> (flickr-duw.19 made libState.q track the box off the library), so coming back to the home draws the shelf filtered by the old query with no results heading to say why. Clear the box, or show the active filter as a chip with an x, when the route is not search.
close_reason: done by flickr-duw.35: the box clears off the route and the library shows its filter as a chip

title: A kid profile's item, work and read routes are filtered like the shelves
description: flickr-duw.22 filters library, search, continue, route and refuses play for a kid profile. GET /api/items/{id}, GET /api/works/{key} and POST /api/items/{id}/read still answer for anything; make them answer not-for-this-profile too so a typed address is no bypass.

title: Hero prefers an entry with a backdrop; search and genre filter the hero row too
description: flickr-duw.18's hero picks strictly resume → recently added → first tile, so with an empty resume shelf a Radiohead cover leads, cropped to a banner. Let the SERVER say which entry leads (a 'hero' relation or field on the library document, preferring one with a backdrop) rather than the client scoring the shelf, and have filterLibrary() hide the hero when a search or genre chip is active.

title: Cards, rows and continue tiles are focusable: tabindex and role on the renderers' tiles
description: flickr-duw.5 added :focus-visible rules, but .card, .cw-card and .item are divs without tabindex (renderers.js card(), memberRow(), continueShelf()), so the keyboard never reaches them. Give them tabindex=0 and role=link/button, and let Enter/Space activate a [data-nav]/[data-act] element in the kernel's click delegation (one keydown listener beside the click one). Test in render_test.mjs that every tile carries tabindex.

title: goldens_shared_test.go sorts before hyper_test.go, so -update needs two runs
description: Both wave-1 server agents hit it: 'go test ./cmd/server -update' copies cmd/server/testdata/hyper to web/testdata/hyper BEFORE hyper_test.go rewrites the server half, because goldens_shared_test.go sorts first. Its header comment claims the opposite order. Fix: rename the file so it sorts last (e.g. zz_goldens_shared_test.go) or have the copy test regenerate rather than copy, and correct the comment.

title: Ten-foot mode: D-pad focus navigation and a TV layout
description: On a TV browser (Android TV, a console) there is no focus management. Do: a data-ten-foot mode toggled from the settings panel (and auto when the viewport is ≥ 1280px and a coarse pointer is absent and the UA is a TV, best effort) with a large type scale, 6-up posters, focus rings that scale the card, and spatial navigation: arrow keys move focus between focusable cards/rows (a small pure function in web/kernel.js or a new web/focus.js that picks the nearest element in the arrow's direction by bounding rect; test it in node with fake rects), Enter activates, Backspace/Escape goes back. Add the new file to sw.js SHELL if created (the integrator bumps CACHE).
acceptance_criteria: With a keyboard only, arrows move focus across the grid and rows, Enter opens, Backspace goes back; the TV layout is legible from a couch.

Then receiver-side stats close the observability loop and chrome://inspect works against the TV.
